name: Heathrow Cargo Tunnel
facts: The Heathrow Cargo Tunnel, opened in December 1968, cost £2 million and was built to link Heathrow’s Terminals 1, 2 and 3 directly with the new cargo terminal, bypassing ground‑level traffic.
Designed as a single‑bore, bi‑directional passage, the tunnel’s 12‑ft lanes and 16‑ft‑6‑in clear height fit snugly within a 33‑ft‑9‑in diameter concrete tube bored through London Clay.
Until 1989, the tunnel uniquely carried London Transport buses, allowing passengers to travel airside without security checks—an unusual loophole that was closed to tighten airport security.
